q: What is the suggested minimum lot size for an R-1 corner lot?
n: Table VIII.G.7 suggests 301 m² for an R-1 inside (regular) lot and 365 m² for an R-1 corner lot. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Table VIII.G.7.

q: What is the suggested minimum lot size for an R-2 inside lot?
n: Table VIII.G.7 suggests 80 m² for a Basic R-2 inside lot. Corner lots are 96 m² and end lots 140 m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Table VIII.G.7.

q: What is the minimum lot area for a medium-cost row house?
n: Under the PD 957 IRR the minimum lot for a medium-cost row house is 50 m². Open-market row houses need 60 m². Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum lot area table.

q: What is the minimum floor area for row houses in open market housing projects?
n: Open-market housing units must have a floor area of at least 42 m². Medium-cost units need 30 m². Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum floor area.

q: What is the minimum lot area for an open-market duplex/single-attached unit?
n: An open-market duplex or single-attached lot needs at least 96 m². Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum lot area table.

q: Under the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Presidential Decree No. 957 governing open market subdivision developments, what is the prescribed minimum lot area for a duplex or single-attached dwelling unit, assuming compliance with standard planning parameters and without deviation through local zoning ordinances?
n: An open-market duplex or single-attached lot needs at least 96 m². Medium-cost needs 72 m². Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008).

q: What is the minimum lot area for an open-market single-detached unit?
n: An open-market single-detached lot needs at least 120 m². Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum lot area table.

q: In the context of open market subdivision development regulated by the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Presidential Decree No. 957, what is the minimum lot area required for a residential unit that is freestanding on all sides, with no party walls shared with adjacent structures, and designed to occupy a single parcel of land exclusively?
n: A freestanding single-detached unit in an open-market subdivision needs at least 120 m². Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008).

q: According to the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of PD 957, what is the minimum area required for a playground in a residential condominium project with up to 10 family dwelling units, and how ts the area adjusted if the number of units exceeds 10?
o: 50 square meters, with 3 sqm added per unit beyond 10
30 square meters, with 2 sqm added per unit beyond 10
75 square meters, with 5 sqm added per unit beyond 10
100 square meters, with 1 sqm added per unit beyond 10
n: Condominium projects provide at least 50 m² of playground for up to 10 family units, plus 3 m² for each additional unit. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), condominium open space.

q: The minimum front setback of dwelling units for both economic and socialized housing shall be:
n: BP 220 sets a minimum front setback of 1.50 m for dwelling units in economic and socialized housing. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, setbacks.

q: What is the minimum frontage for a single-detached corner lot in an open market and medium-cost housing project?
n: A single-detached corner lot in open-market or medium-cost housing needs at least 12 m of frontage. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum lot frontage.

q: What is the minimum lot frontage for a single-detached regular lot under open market and medium-cost housing projects?
n: A regular single-detached lot needs at least 10 m of frontage. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum lot frontage.

q: What is the minimum frontage for a duplex/single-attached lot in an open market and medium-cost housing project?
n: A duplex or single-attached lot in open-market or medium-cost housing needs at least 8 m of frontage. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), minimum lot frontage.

q: Considering BP 220 only, what is the minimum frontage for a duplex/single-attached lot?
n: Under BP 220 a duplex or single-attached lot needs at least 6 m of frontage, for economic and socialized alike. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Table on minimum lot frontage.

q: The amount paid to the architect, in percentage of the agreed professional fee, upon completion of the contract documents phase and not more than 15 days after submission of the documents to the owner.
n: When the contract documents are submitted, payments rise to a total of 90% of the professional fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: The down payment upon signing of the service agreement is:
n: On signing the service agreement, the owner pays 5% of the fee as the down payment (mobilization). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.1.

q: Upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase. how much of the Professional Fee should the Architect receive under the Standards of Professional Practice (SPP)?
n: Completing schematic design earns a further 15% of the fee, bringing the total to 20%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: What is the minimum fee for post-construction services?
n: Post-construction services under value pricing are 4% to 6% of gross rental, a minimum of 4%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: What is the maximum fee for post-construction services?
n: The maximum for post-construction services is 6% of gross rental. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: For a ₱10 million agreed professional fee for a project, how much is the engagement or acceptance fee?
n: The engagement (acceptance) fee is 5% of the professional fee: 5% × ₱10,000,000 = ₱500,000. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.1.

q: A type of service wherein all engineering and engineering specialist consultant fees are excluded. In such a situation, the architect remains as the lead or prime professional for the project.
n: DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services) excludes all engineering fees. The architect still leads the project. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: A type of service where there is a contract between the Architect and the Owner. and sub- contractor contracts between the Architect and the other professionals working with the Architect.
n: When the architect contracts with the owner and subcontracts the engineers, the service is architectural and engineering (DAEDS), with the architect as prime professional. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (modes of engagement).

q: A type of service wherein the architect and the engineering and allied professionals directly sign contracts with the owner.
n: In direct hiring, the architect and each engineering and allied professional sign separate contracts with the owner. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (modes of engagement).

q: How much is the recommended percentage of PCC for the RPF for a Regular Design Service of a residential building, for DADS and DAEDS respectively?
n: Residential buildings (Group 4) carry an RPF of 6% of PCC for DADS and 10% for DAEDS. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: What is the RPF for residential projects (DADS, DAEDS)?
n: Residential (Group 4): 6% for DADS and 10% for DAEDS. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: Recommended professional fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services for Residential projects
n: The DAEDS fee for residential projects is 10% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: Recommended professional fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services for Monumental projects
n: The DAEDS fee for monumental buildings (Group 5) is 12% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5.

q: What is the recommended professional fee for monumental projects (DADS, DAEDS)?
n: Monumental buildings (Group 5): 7.5% for DADS and 12% for DAEDS. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5.

q: According to the Standards of Professional Practice (SPP), what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS) for a condominium project?
n: Residential condominiums are Group 2. The DADS fee is 60% of the 6% DAEDS rate, so 3.6% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2.

q: According to the Standards of Professional Practice (SPP), what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) for a church project classified under Group 2?
n: Churches are Group 2. The DAEDS fee is 6% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2.

q: What is the recommended professional fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services for a supermarket with a cost of ₱30M?
n: Supermarkets are Group 2. For PCC of ₱50 million or less, the DAEDS fee is 6%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2.

q: What is the recommended professional fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services for a gymnasium with a cost of ₱50M?
n: Gymnasiums are Group 3 (exceptional complexity). The DAEDS fee is 7%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3.

q: What is the recommended professional fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services for an auditorium with a cost of ₱50M?
n: Auditoriums are Group 3. The DAEDS fee is 7%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3.

q: In the context of Specialized Architectural Services as defined by PRBOA Resolution No. 06, Series of 2016, which term refers to the total cost of all fixtures and accessories for architectural interiors, acoustics, lighting, site development civil works, and landscaping (including hardscape and softscape) designed, specified, or procured by the Specialist Architect or Specialist Consultants for the Owner/Client and used or installed in the project?
n: For specialized services, the Cost of the Work covers all fixtures and accessories for interiors, acoustics, lighting, site works and landscaping that the specialist designs or procures. Source: PRBOA Resolution No. 06, Series of 2016 (2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203).

q: How much is the RPF for the Regular Design of an airport with a PCC of ₱375,000,000.00?
n: Airports are Group 3, with a DAEDS fee of 7%: 7% × ₱375,000,000 = ₱26.25 million. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3.

q: What is the best method of compensation for post-construction services?
n: Post-construction (building administration) services are best paid as a percentage of gross income or rental (value pricing, 4–6%). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.

q: A proposed facility will house elderly residents who require continuous supervision and assistance. Most occupants are non-ambulatory and will reside in the building full-time. Under the National Building Code of the Philippines (NBCP), what is the correct occupancy classification for this type of nursing home?
n: A nursing home housing non-ambulatory residents full-time is Group D, Division 2 (institutional: homes for the aged and similar). Source: NBC (PD 1096), Sec. 701 (occupancy classification).

q: For a 7-storey nursing home with a floor area of 950 sqm, the prevailing construction cost is ₱50,000.00/sqm. What is the project construction cost?
n: The Project Construction Cost is the floor area multiplied by the unit construction cost: PCC = 950 m² × ₱50,000/m² = ₱47,500,000. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (PCC definition).

q: For the same nursing home (PCC ₱47,500,000), what is the RPF for architectural and engineering services (DAEDS)?
n: Health facilities are Group 3, with a DAEDS fee of 7%: 7% × ₱47.5M = ₱3,325,000. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3.

q: For the same nursing home, what is the RPF for architecture only (DADS)?
n: DADS for Group 3 is 60% of 7%, so 4.2%: 4.2% × ₱47.5M = ₱1,995,000. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3.

q: Should the owner decide to halt the project upon completion of the Design Development Phase, what percentage of the total RPF should the architect have already received?
n: Payments through design development: 5% (signing) + 15% (schematic) + 20% (design development) = 40% of the fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Method of compensation for intermittent services given at intervals over a given period of time.
n: A retainer pays a set amount at regular intervals for services given intermittently over a period. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: A method of compensation which can be used when the scope of services required can be clearly and fully defined at the outset of the project. The agreement should contain a clearly stated time limit during which the service/s will be performed.
n: A lump sum (fixed fee) suits work whose scope can be fully defined at the outset, with a stated time limit. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: Type of construction contract with a fixed amount.
n: A lump-sum (fixed-price) contract has a fixed amount for the stated work. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines; RA 9184 IRR (contract types).

q: Recommended method of compensation when an architect is asked to do an ocular inspection.
n: Short, one-off tasks like an ocular inspection are paid per diem (plus reimbursable expenses). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).
